key_concepts: Ray diagramming is a method for locating and describing qualitative image characteristics
A P-F ray travels parallel to the principal axis and refracts through the real focus F
A V ray passes through the optical center without being refracted
An F-P ray passes through the virtual focus F' before the lens and emerges parallel to the
The image is located where refracted rays intersect
If refracted rays do not intersect, they are extended to locate a virtual image
An object beyond 2F' forms a real, inverted, reduced image between F and 2F
An object at 2F' forms a real, inverted, same-size image at 2F
An object between F' and 2F' forms a real, inverted, enlarged image beyond 2F
An object at F' produces no image because refracted rays are parallel
An object between the lens and F' forms a virtual, erect, enlarged image
